note:
Emma Taylor, a widow living on her own means, with her two grown daughters, a young visitor and two servants at 11 Newcastle Drive (#213) on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the six was in the record, and 11 Newcastle Drive held only 1921 (the Topham household), so 1891 is free.

She had left within seven years: Wright's Directory prints 'Miss Louisa H. Topham; Joseph R. Topham, of J. R. Tpm & Bro.' at number 11 in 1898-99, and Joseph R. Topham holds it through 1915-16 and is there on the 1921 return. There is no 1894-95 line for the number, so nothing places her after this census.

Several Taylors are already in the record - at Castlethorpe, 9 Hamilton Drive, 43 Lenton Road and Fairlawn - and none matches this widow or her daughters on name and year together, so all three are created new. Kate Gladys King, the ten-year-old visitor from Bath, is joined to nobody: the return gives no relationship beyond visitor. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way. **The number is confirmed by the schedule itself.** A. Hagues has since supplied the page: schedules 84 to 88 are headed 13, 11, 9, 7 and 5 **Newcastle drive** in the enumerator's own hand. Although this street had been Pelham Terrace, the 1891 numbers on it are Newcastle Drive numbers. See [[newcastle-drive-pelham-terrace-numbers]].
source: 1891 census, 11 Newcastle Drive, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1898-99, page 109 (Leicester Special Collections id 165285).
